newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ s/adj retail sales worth NZ$3.19 bln in Feb-SNZ.
newsitem.headline: NZ s/adj retail sales worth NZ$3.19 bln in Feb-SNZ.

text.p: New Zealand seasonally adjusted retail sales fell by 2.4 percent in February, and were worth NZ$3.19 billion, Statistics New Zealand (SNZ) said on Wednesday.
Excluding both automotive storetypes, seasonally adjusted sales were down 2.6 percent in the month, to $2.21 billion.
Fourteen of the 15 storetypes recorded falls in seasonally adjusted sales in February, led by furniture and floorcovering stores (down 10.9 percent) and hardware stores (down 9.4 percent).
Cafe, restaurant and takeaway outlets recorded the only increase, up 0.7 percent.
SNZ said the underlying trend in retail sales fell 0.1 percent in the month.
Total actual retail sales for February were $2.99 billion, which was $107 million or 3.5 percent below those in February 1996.
Actual retail sales excluding both automotive storetypes were $2.06 billion in February, a fall of 1.2 percent from sales in February 1996.
Eleven storetypes recorded falls in actual sales when compared with a year earlier.

The largest fall was in clothing and softgoods outlets (down 11.2 percent), followed by motor vehicle retailing outlets (down 10.5 percent), furniture and floorcovering stores (down 5.9 percent) and accommodation, hotel and liquor outlets and motor vehicle services (both down 4.9 percent).
February 1997 had one less trading day than February 1996, which SNZ said may have contributed to the fall in retail sales across many of the storetypes.

Motor vehicle retailing outlets contributed 58 percent, or $62 million, to the $107 million annual fall in actual retail sales, while motor vehicle services contributed a further 20 percent ($21 million).
Total sales in the South Island fell 3.6 percent in the year to February, while North Island sales were down 3.4 percent.
SNZ said credit card billings to New Zealand card holders in February was 10.1 percent higher than in February 1996.
The provisional number of building permits for new dwelling units was 12.2 percent below February 1996, which SNZ said might impact on the furniture, household appliances and hardware stores.
